talks.title: Recon2024-AlessandroDiFederico PietroFezzardi PathOfRevngance FromRawBytesToCodeQLOnDecompiledCode
talks.teaser: Provides recon2024-AlessandroDiFederico PietroFezzardi PathOfRevngance FromRawBytesToCodeQLOnDecompiledCode and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary: Alessandro Di Federico and Pietro Fezzardi present rev.ng, an open-source binary framework that lifts many ISAs through QEMU-style front ends into LLVM IR for optimization and decompilation instead of emulating code at runtime. They introduce YAML project models, CLI and HTTP daemon workflows, analyses that auto-fill segments and prototypes, and LLVM snapshots that collapse stack traffic into readable IR. Live demos lift raw x86 bytes and optimized ELFs, run KLEE symbolic execution on lifted bitcode to catch inter-procedural use-after-free bugs, feed the same rev.ng C output into Clang Static Analyzer and CodeQL, and highlight automatic struct recovery that prettifies linked-list traversals. Closing remarks note supported import formats, ongoing performance work toward Ghidra-class speed, mass regression testing, and a commercial VS Code UI plus collaboration hub.

talks.title: Andrea Allievi&Satoshi Tanda-HypervisorEnforced Paging Translation....
talks.teaser: Provides andrea Allievi&Satoshi Tanda-HypervisorEnforced Paging Translation and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary: Andrea Allievi and Satoshi Tanda explain how Windows counters kernel data remapping attacks that bypass Kernel Data Protection by retargeting page tables without writing protected globals. They recap CET shadow stacks and PAC on Arm64, then demo zeroing the CI Options variable through page-table remapping until Hypervisor-Enforced Paging Translation blocks the change. They describe how HEPAC clones nested page tables, maps them read-only to the guest, and routes selected kernel translations through hypervisor-managed tables, including reuse of MMP data as HEPAC roots and the multi-year removal of session space. They note gaps such as unprotected user runtime drivers and discuss TLB flush and performance trade-offs.

talks.title: Bálint Varga-Perke Control Flow Intergrity on IBM i
talks.teaser: Reviews strategic developments and core technical considerations regarding Control Flow Integrity on IBM iSeries platforms.
talks.summary: Bálint Varga of Silent Signal unpacks control-flow and memory protections on IBM i at security level 40, starting with single-level-store addressing and MI bytecode before native POWER code. He shows straightforward C buffer overflows that corrupt adjacent integers, explains how tagged thick pointers and LQ plus TXBR trap pairs block jumps into data, and maps TD mask pairs that confine pointer arithmetic within 40-bit segments. Using SST dumps, save-file extraction, and a Kaitai parser wired into Ghidra, he extends disassembly for POWER AS instructions, patches a TD check to wander into the QSECOFR address space, and demonstrates out-of-context calls that hijack nearby function pointers to run system(). He notes logical bugs dominate real deployments, speculates on TOCTOU via reused SLS slots, and warns that tampered save files could ship unprotected machine code if CRC algorithms are cracked.
